title: Paryantapañcāśikā
text:
**invocation**
Homage to the blessed Gaṇapati.
**1**
I take up in study that unutterable Speech, brimming over with the repose of the infinite powers contained within it from beginning to end — the very Heart of the all-pervading Lord.
**2**
That alone is the God {{bhairava:the terrible-blissful Absolute Śiva of Trika}}, and all the gods are made of That. She too is that very Bhairavī, and being and non-being alike are made of That.
**3**
That alone is Bhairava-knowledge, and ignorance too is made of That. That, indeed, is the established conclusion of Bhairava — and even the opponent's thesis [pūrvapakṣa] is made of That.
**4**
That in which the six paths [{{adhvan:path/way; the six cosmic paths}}] become one — that is the Bhairava-state: the ineffable supreme goal that lies at the culmination [{{paryanta:the ultimate limit / culmination where all tantras converge}}] of all the tantras.
**5**
She is that in whom will, knowledge, and true action [{{icchā-jñāna-kriyā:will, knowledge, action — the three powers}}] lie immersed, having for their very being nothing but consciousness-bliss; she is the Heart of the God of gods, Bhairava — the undivided ground.
**6**
By the innate nature of consciousness, this God, the Lord, reflecting upon himself by his own self [{{vimarśa / vimṛśan:self-reflective awareness of consciousness}}], takes on the stages ranging from the 'unsupported' [anāśrita] down to the level of earth.
**7**
Therein, from the Lord's single vibration [{{spanda:the subtle creative vibration of consciousness}}] whose nature is signifier and signified — each unfolding in a sequence of gross, subtle, and supreme manifestation — arises the sixfold character of the path [ṣaḍvidha-adhvan].
**8**
The sequence [krama] whose nature is space and time is the very life-breath of differentiation among the [individual] awarenesses; through this rupture the knower is rendered into a manifoldness of varied appearances.
**9**
There are, indeed, two modes here, by the distinction of pure and impure: purity is the sinking of the externalized objects back into one's own pure I-ness [{{ahaṃ / aham:the pure 'I' / supreme subjectivity}}].
**10**
Impurity, by contrast, is when [the objects], though submerged, do not thus find repose in the Heart. And even within this interval there may be endless gradations of states, by degrees of more and less.
**11**
In the manifesting of knowers, whose knowables are [each] fitting and unfitting [to them], the shared and the separate modes split apart into knower and known [mātṛ and meya].
**12**
That creation whose manifestation is vivid and free of thought-construct [{{vikalpa:discursive, dichotomizing thought-construct}}] is held to be the Śāmbhava creation; in the non-dual fashioning of the self, the Self alone is made the instrument.
**13**
The power of consciousness, whose essence is action and knowledge, by reason of its weaving out differentiation, reaches the level of kalā and vidyā and then comes forth again in the bursting-forth of difference.
**14**
When that very [power], from whose activity arise the thought-constructs that are the multitude of means-of-knowledge and intellections — its activity now fragmented and re-fragmented — rises up as the effort of knowing,
**15**
having attained the condition of an action-intellect and its senses, then it is called the bound soul [{{paśu:the bound, fettered soul, literally 'beast'}}]. Thus, by his own will, the Blessed Lord Bhairava lets himself be measured out [into limitation].

title: Paryantapañcāśikā
text:
**16**
And that Power, becoming limited in her operation, follows after him; from his [progressively] contracting condition through the states of Vidyeśa, Sadākhya, and Śiva, [he] comes down into a knowership identified with body, vital breath, intellect, and the void.
**17**
His particular [private] creation is the manifold thought-construction of this and that, dependent upon him who is conditioned by the latent traces arisen from the Śaiva [cosmic] emission.
**18**
This very knower, of just such a fashion, in the festival of [self-]apprehension, abides undistracted in his own Self — non-conceptual and made of consciousness.
**19**
My child, behold: it is you alone — the universe, when truly known, is made of That, non-dual with awareness, for everything else is trifling and unreal.
**20**
By what means could this Reality be reached, since nothing other than it exists at all? Therefore they declare it to be the means-less means [{{ananyopāya / anupāya:the means-less means; the Self as sole means}}], the Self-as-means.
**21**
Withdrawing thought from everything and cultivating [the awareness] 'I' [{{ahaṃ / aham:the pure 'I' / supreme subjectivity}}], one attains a non-conceptual, directly-evident awareness of oneself.
**22**
Even while taking up endless forms of just such extent, [that self-awareness remains] of a single character; entering into that awareness of oneself, one should construct no thought-constructs at all.
**23**
Plunging into Vyomeśvarī, the consciousness that is the Self — that great lake brimming with the currents of the four streams beginning with {{khecarī:the sky-roving power/goddess of consciousness}} — one should drown [therein] all that is inert.
**24**
Performing the five acts [{{pañcakṛtya:the five acts — creation, maintenance, withdrawal, concealment, grace}}] in the sequence of emission, preservation, withdrawal, concealment, and grace, one should hold the conviction 'I am Śiva.'
**25**
Or by the sequence of casting-forth, knowing, enumerative reflection [prasaṃkhyāna], passage, and resonance [nāda], having gathered those [acts] into the Self through the mouth of the teacher, one becomes fulfilled.
**26**
Having so determined: 'I am Bhairava, the Self of all, and these manifold modes of the universe are mine alone — just as the wavering tongues of flame belong to fire, and the radiance to the sun' —
**27**
'I am the One, possessed of the modes of knower, cognition, means-of-knowledge, and known; in the form of pure awareness and the rest, I am the fourteen [powers] beginning with the {{khecarī:the sky-roving power of consciousness}}.'
**28**
Contemplating bondage and liberation in their modes of difference and non-difference, through the firm trust 'I am Bhairava,' one should attain the supreme autonomy.
**29**
The inner act and the outer act of the Self you bring about free of temporal sequence and dependent on nothing else — for you are brimming with sovereign power [{{anuttara:the Unsurpassable / Absolute, the 'a' of Trika}}].
**30**
The coupling [{{yāmala / saṃghaṭṭa:the paired union / fusion of Śiva and Śakti}}] of Śiva and Śakti is the pairing of repose and arising, whose essence is the Anuttara and the emission [{{visarga:emission / creative outpouring, also the phoneme ḥ}}]; and in the interval between them lie the other powers.
**31**
Bliss, will, lordship, and opening-forth [unmeṣa] — and a [relative] deficiency belonging to lordship and to will: through these two [arises], by the distinction of indistinct and distinct, the surging-forth of the knowable [vedya] from awareness.

title: Paryantapañcāśikā
text:
**32**
And from Bliss and the Anuttara comes the state of conjunction; then cognition, which has become the very life-breath of the knowables. Such is that full body of Bhairava.
**33**
This surging-forth of the knowable, abiding as one within will and within lordship, in its gross aspect becomes the set of five elements beginning with earth;
**34**
and in its subtle aspect, the set of five subtle-elements [tanmātras] beginning with smell; and then, in its instrumental aspect, through contact, the twice-five [ten] sense-organs.
**35**
By the veiling of knowable-ness, in the sequence whereby knower-ness shines forth, [it becomes] the state of mind, ego, and intellect of these [organs]; in their undivided condition, primordial-nature [prakṛti]; and the state of person [puruṣa] — these [last two] being that in reference to which there are contraction and expansion.
**36**
They came to be from the conjunction of the desired [object], which is twofold in form and shares in both [knower and known] — from the opening-forth whose essence is will, [and again] otherwise from what is joined with the Anuttara.
**37**
The four powers that reside within this person, sustaining within him both the sky of consciousness and the ground of inert matter, are made of māyā, [poised] like Triśaṅku [between the two].
**38**
From the power of will, which is threefold, three other powers arose; and then this emission [visarga] became exceedingly distinct through the expansion of what is to be created.
**39**
Having created this from the mutual commingling of the powers of the Self, an inner agitation [kṣobha] arises; nothing comes to be outside, apart from this emission.
**40**
All this manifold, while it exists, again and again comes to rest in Anuttara-Bhairava through the gateways of will and the rest — and from there alone it is emitted forth once more.
**41**
The supreme consciousness — the supreme [Speech], {{parā / paśyantī / madhyamā / vaikharī:the four ascending levels of Speech}} — is the Self's self-touch of the infinite meanings dissolved within it; she, who bears all in a single act, is the mantric Speech and pure agency.
**42**
She draws Time of her own accord — Time that flows threefold, runs in three paths, and stands in three [stations] — outward, and from there back into the Self: thus is the blessed Parā the Drawer-of-Time [Kālakarṣiṇī].
**43**
Parāparā is the contemplation of the undivided being [now] internalized though [seemingly] differentiated; that same agency, resting on the lordly state of that very [Parā], is Paśyantī [the 'Seeing' Speech].
**44**
Madhyamā [the 'Middle' Speech] is sequential, gross, abiding in the inner faculty, its expressible content split apart by thought-construction, divided by the operation of the vital breath.
**45**
Through abiding in the condition of its own latent dispositions, even in the two prior states there can be the limitedness of the māyā-bound measurer; and the sequence of Paśyantī too is atom-fine [aṇu].
**46**
Entering in turn into those two states — the quiescent [śānta] and the thought-constructing [vikalpa] — the blessed one beholds, with wonder, the full expanse of his own self-awareness.
**47**
She, having for her essence the person's exertion through the striking of the points and organs of articulation, is Vaikharī [the 'Uttered' Speech], whose operations are these [articulate sounds] that fall within the range of hearing.
**48**
By means of these [forms of Speech], reciprocal discourse — whose essence is the transmission of knowledge from one to another — comes about, whether ordinary or scriptural, hemmed in by manifold contractions.

title: Paryantapañcāśikā
text:
**49**
Thus, the presiding goddesses of these [phonematic] classes — the deities headed by Māheśvarī — never consume [i.e., devour into limitation] the one who knows the pervasion of Speech, even in the waking state.
**50**
The means must be firmly grasped; the goal to be attained is the Bhairava-state. That very self-awareness, which contains all means within it [{{ananyopāya / anupāya:the means-less means; the Self as sole means}}] — that alone one should enter into.
**51**
I take refuge in the Anuttara radiance — brimming with the infinite signified and signifier contained within it from beginning to end, the secret of all mantras and mudrās [{{anuttara:the Unsurpassable / Absolute, the 'a' of Trika}}].
**52**
Victorious are the gurus of old, their hearts undivided from Śambhu, who through an absorption from which there is no [returning] re-emergence attained the consummate wealth of the ultimate goal [{{paryanta:the ultimate limit / culmination where all tantras converge}}].
**colophon-1**
Homage to Śiva.
**colophon-2**
Here is completed this composition of the venerable master Abhinavagupta, called the Paryantapañcāśikā ["The Fifty [Verses] on the Ultimate Goal"].
